title: Diagnostic yield of ambulatory patch monitor in Emergency Department syncope patients
author: Christopher J. Weir
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bgtfjwjn
materials: Biomarkers: Previous work on cardiac biomarkers by our group has shown they may have good prognostic value inthe ED assessment of syncope [1,21,22].In the process ofderiving and validatingthe ROSE (Risk Stratification of Syncope in the ED) clinical decision rule,we demonstrated that plasma brain natriuretic peptide (BNP) concentrations≥300 ng/L were an independent predictor of serious outcome and death with an odds ratio (OR) of 7.3 and a negative predictive value (NPV) of 95.4% (93.0-97.0) [1]. Furthermore, we measured troponin I concentrations using acontemporarysensitive assay(ARCHITEC STAT troponin I assay; Abbott Laboratories, Abbott Park, IL) in 338 of 528 syncope patients admitted to hospital as part of the ROSE study. Troponin was measureable above the limit of detection (10 ng/L) in 77%of patients and above the limit of quantification (50 ng/L; coefficient of variation (CV) 98% of healthy persons and has the potential to greatly improve discrimination in patients with syncope. Unexplained syncope is rarely due to Myocardial Infarction (MI) [22].We hypothesise that elevated troponin and BNP concentrations in patients with syncope are likely to reflect secondary myocardial injury due to myocardial oxygen supply and demand imbalance or reduced cardiac output in severe arrhythmia or structural abnormality.
4. Research methods; Study design: Prospective cohort study.
Study setting: Single centre, teaching hospital ED.

steps.title: Identify eligible syncope patients
steps.instruction: Screen all Emergency Department (ED) attendances for patients aged ≥ 16 years who present within 6 hours of a transient loss of consciousness (syncope) that remains unexplained after initial ED assessment.

steps.title: Check inclusion and exclusion criteria
steps.instruction: Confirm the patient meets all inclusion criteria (100 consecutive eligible patients, age ≥ 16 years, presentation ≤ 6 h after syncope) and does not meet any exclusion criteria (obvious underlying cause, alcohol/drug‑induced TLOC, seizure with >15 min post‑ictal phase, stroke/TIA, head trauma with TLOC, hypoglycaemia, lack of capacity, prior study enrolment, custody, or any of the listed obvious causes such as documented arrhythmia on ED ECG, pulmonary embolism, postural hypotension >20 mmHg, myocardial infarction, cerebrovascular bleed, etc.).

steps.title: Obtain informed consent
steps.instruction: Assess the patient’s capacity, provide the Patient Information Sheet and allow 10‑15 min (or up to 1 hour if needed) for questions, then obtain a written signature on the study consent form. Document the capacity assessment. Do not approach patients lacking capacity.

steps.title: Collect baseline clinical data
steps.instruction: Complete the paper Data Collection Form (DCF) in the ED, recording demographics, history, examination findings, 12‑lead ECG, radiology, standard laboratory results, and patient contact details. Archive the paper DCF for up to 5 years and enter all fields into the password‑protected electronic database on the NHS Lothian ‘S’ drive.

steps.title: Obtain research blood samples
steps.instruction: Three hours after admission, draw two research venous samples: 2.7 ml (≈ ½ teaspoon) EDTA tube for BNP measurement using the ALERE TRIAGE point‑of‑care BNP test (ALERE, San Diego, USA) and 4.7 ml (≈ just under 1 teaspoon) Li‑Heparin Gel tube for high‑sensitivity troponin I measurement using the ARCHITECT STAT assay in the Royal Infirmary of Edinburgh (RIE) laboratory. Store both samples in an annotated biobank for unlimited future testing. Do not report these results to the treating clinician.

steps.title: Apply ZIO® XT Patch
steps.instruction: A trained research team member places the ZIO® XT Patch (iRhythm Technologies) on the patient’s chest in the ED. The patch is water‑resistant, lead‑free, and has a button for symptom capture. Instruct the patient to wear it continuously for up to 14 days (2 weeks).

steps.title: Provide patient diary and return materials
steps.instruction: Give the participant a diary to record any symptomatic episodes (light‑headedness, dizziness, syncope/presyncope) and a patch‑satisfaction questionnaire. Supply a pre‑paid envelope addressed to the research team for returning the patch after the monitoring period. Provide contact details of the PATCH‑ED research team for any patch‑related problems.

steps.title: Monitor and retrieve the patch
steps.instruction: Allow the patient to wear the patch for the full 14‑day period, recording events in the diary. At the end of the monitoring period, the patient mails the patch back in the supplied envelope. Upon receipt, forward the patch to the iRhythm Clinical Centre for processing by a certified electrocardiographic technician.

steps.title: Obtain and store patch report
steps.instruction: Access the completed patch report via the secure website www.zioreports.com using the study‑only login. Download the PDF and save it on the password‑protected ‘S’ drive. Review the report immediately.

steps.title: Act on significant arrhythmia findings
steps.instruction: If the report shows any serious significant arrhythmia—defined as ventricular fibrillation, ventricular tachycardia > 120 bpm lasting ≥ 30 s, symptomatic ventricular tachycardia, complete or 3rd‑degree AV block, symptomatic 2nd‑degree type II block, pause > 6 s, or symptomatic bradycardia lasting ≥ 30 s—contact the participant promptly and refer them to the Royal Infirmary of Edinburgh cardiac electrophysiology service.

steps.title: Conduct 90‑day follow‑up
steps.instruction: At 90 days post‑presentation, review the patient’s hospital and General Practitioner electronic records to determine diagnostic yield, arrhythmia prevalence, and any serious outcomes. No additional ISD linkage is required.

steps.title: Record and report adverse events
steps.instruction: Monitor for adverse events related to the blood draw (infection, haematoma) or patch (skin irritation). Report any event meeting the Serious Adverse Event (SAE) criteria (death, life‑threatening, hospitalization or prolongation, persistent disability, congenital anomaly) to the sponsor within 24 hours according to SOP CR006. Non‑serious events are recorded in the study database.

steps.title: Maintain data security and retention
steps.instruction: Store paper CRFs for up to 5 years, keep the electronic database on the secure password‑protected ‘S’ drive, and retain all bio‑resource blood samples indefinitely. Ensure identifiable data are kept in a separate locked filing cabinet accessible only to authorized research staff. Anonymised data may be kept indefinitely for future research.
